reason: Cercocarpus styles lengthen into plumose tails in fruit; 'style very slender, in fruit 3-4 cm long' is style length 3-4 cm during the fruit stage.
Follicles are fruits; 'Follicles red' is fruit colour red. A follicle-specific PO class would be finer but fruit is not wrong.

target: elliptic to ovate-lanceolate (upper endpoint is the compound shape ovate-lanceolate, between ovate and lanceolate PATO_0001877)
fix: Hyphenated compound shape words after 'to' (ovate-lanceolate, oblong-elliptic) are cut to their first half. Read the whole compound as the endpoint (intermediate of both components), not just its first word.
reason: The source's upper end of the range is ovate-lanceolate, not ovate; recording 'ovate' widens the range to a shape the flora does not give.
Male inflorescences much branched: inflorescence branched, with the male context recorded.

fix: Note: 'abaxially glabrous but veins puberulent' carries an exception for the veins; ideally the exception is kept (veins puberulent annotated separately) so the glabrous claim reads as 'except veins'.
reason: The flora says the leaf blade is glabrous on the abaxial surface; substitution to leaf lamina abaxial epidermis is right.
Pinnae (leaflets) ovate, broadly lanceolate or lanceolate: shape alternatives at taxon level; ovate and broadly lanceolate are rendered correctly (the third alternative belongs to the same list).
'leaves white- or yellowish-tomentose beneath' = abaxial leaf surface tomentose; 'beneath' is correctly mapped to the abaxial epidermis.

fix: 'style distinct' (also 'style evident', 'style obvious') in a description of a single gynoecium means the style is well developed and visible, as opposed to stigma sessile; it is not 'free from' another part. Map 'distinct' to free only when it is said of several organs relative to each other (petals distinct, stamens distinct).
reason: Rhaphidophora has a single style on the ovary followed by its length (ca. 1 cm); 'distinct' contrasts with a sessile stigma, not with fusion.
'folioles ± nombreuses' = leaflets present, many; the ± softens the count word but does not change the reading.
Capsules described in the immature state are present; the immature state is recorded as context of the bearer.

fix: A face adverb ('adaxially', 'abaxially', 'above', 'beneath') governs the comma-separated qualities that follow it up to the next face adverb; 'abaxially pale green, rather shiny, adaxially deep green, not shiny' gives shiny abaxially and not shiny adaxially.
reason: Without the adaxial scope the annotation says the whole blade is not shiny, but the flora says the abaxial side is rather shiny.
FNA gives length × width; leaf blade length 1-5 cm (the roundish blade can be wider than long).
Stamens ca. 3 mm at anthesis: stamen length 3 mm at the anthesis stage. The 'ca.' is not visible in these fields; it should be kept as approximately if the record drops it.

target: position/whole: basal leaf (rosette leaf PO_0000014 or a basal-leaf position context)
fix: 'blades of basal leaves' / 'blades of cauline leaves': the 'of X leaves' phrase restricts the bearer to that kind of leaf and must be kept as the position or whole slot.
reason: The flora gives ovate-orbiculate only for the basal leaves; Doronicum cauline leaves have a different shape, so the bare 'leaf lamina' claim is false.
Involucre awns reddish: awn colour red, approximately (the -ish suffix).

fix: In Carex descriptions in the North American Flora (NAF), the run 'broadly obovoid, many-ribbed, olive-green, … beaked' describes the perigynium (the achene is described later, 'achenes …'). Map it to perigynium, not fruit. Also 'sub-' (submembranaceous) should carry the approximately qualifier (docs/odp/01).
reason: The subject of this clause is the perigynium (the achene is said to be enveloped in the perigynium body); also 'submembranaceous' is only somewhat membranous, but no qualifier is recorded.
Petals ± spreading: petal spreading, approximately.
(0.1-)1.5-8(-10) dm converts to 15-80 cm with extremes 1 and 100 cm; plant height.
'seeds transverse, flattened' = seed flattened.
Leaf margin with 18-55(-90) teeth per side: tooth count on the leaf margin, each side, max extreme 90.
Leaves 0.5-5 cm: leaf length.

fix: 'X awnless' must keep X as the whole of the absent awn; a bare 'awn absent' at genus level is false when other parts in the same text are aristate.
reason: In Elionurus only the upper glume and upper lemma are awnless; the pedicellate spikelet may be shortly aristate, so 'awn absent' without its whole is false.
Stems slender.
Branches ± whorled: branch whorled, approximately.
Achenes obovoid-orbicular: a shape between obovoid and orbicular. Mixing a 3-D term with a 2-D one is common in floras and still says what the source means.

target: leaf lamina tip (PO_0025589) / leaflet apex (acumen) with leaflet as whole
fix: 'apex acuminate, the acumen acute or spathulate': qualities after 'the acumen' belong to the acumen (the drawn-out tip), not to the leaflet; the antecedent noun of 'the acumen/the tip/the apex' must become the bearer.
reason: The flora says the acumen's tip is acute or spathulate; the leaflet itself is ovate-oblong or oblong.
Plants ca. 20 cm tall: plant height 20 cm (approximately).

target: awn column (lower, twisted part of the awn below the first bend) with awn (PO_0025349) as whole
fix: In Stipa and other grass awns, 'column X cm to first bend' and 'bristle X cm' measure parts of the awn; they must not be given to the awn itself (whose length here is 9-20 cm).
reason: The awn is 9-20 cm; 1.5-1.8 cm is the column to the first bend, so 'awn length 1.5-1.8 cm' contradicts the flora.
Sori very numerous: sorus present, many.

target: position: middle one of a row (middle pinnae), not median (FLOPO_0991381)
fix: FLOPO_0991381 'median' is a PATO position (PATO_0000140) for the midline of the body, so it cannot express 'the middle members of a series'. 'middle ones' / 'middle pinnae' should get a context class for 'middle of a series' (like the existing distal/proximal handling); map such phrases to it rather than to median.
reason: Earlier I marked this correct, reading FLOPO_0991381 as 'middle'. It is actually 'median' (the midline). The flora means the middle pinnae of the row (10-20 cm long), so the position slot says the wrong thing.
